I absolutely love the concept of "machine that pokes holes in reality". It's sad that so many people don't get it and think it's some sort a clichéd insanity ray. So I will upvote it and hope that others start seeing it the same way as I do: an excellent, original and expertly written scip.

However: I can't understand the logic behind the Leading scientist's plan: "Oh, this thing can do pretty serious, permanent damage to the very tissue of reality even when callibrated to low levels of power… LET'S JUMP TO MAXIMUM AND SHOOT THAT SHIT! YIPPIE-KAY-YAY MOTHERFUCKER!"

I would, if given the chance, demote that man to D class. Because "altering the world forever due to pure simple ineptitude" is not funny.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
1, It communicates by text. I felt that the detail was inconsequential, so I left it out. The important detail is that it messaged us on the O5's secure network. The O5's are never supposed to have contact with SCPs. That is a massive security breach.

2, The Foundation does not know where it came from. There are a few possibilities. It could be from an alternate present. It could be from a doomed future where the Foundation built it and sent it back in time to stop some sort of apocalypse. It could be a Trojan Horse. I'm sure that there are other possibilities, but the risk of it being a Trojan Horse merits not asking it too many questions. The Foundation doesn't want to tip its hand. Personally, I felt that the uncertain origin was the most dangerous.

3, There are large unpopulated areas in the world. Australia, Antarctica, northeastern Russia, and the Sahara Desert come to mind. It's possible to find a circle 4km across that no one would notice if anything weird happened. There's also nuclear testing sites. As for the exact way that it works, Felgraf and I tried to make it clear that while the desired outcome (unless it's a Trojan Horse) is that it insanes people, it does so by poking holes in reality at precise locations. Small holes plug up really quickly. In the case of a maximum intensity firing, what was observed was the "shadows" of something on the other side that made it through. When the hole closed up, the shadow was no longer cast through the hole. However, it didn't heal perfectly. There's scar tissue in our reality around the affected are. The real problem is that the Foundation can't safely run tests to find out more. As such, the Foundation can only speculate what's on the other side of those holes.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This is kind of a great SCP overall, but I have three major issues with it:

1) How does it "communicate"? I mean, does it use actual words? If so, are they auditory or visual? If not, what sort of signals does it use? The fact that it has made reports via an "information relay system" doesn't tell me much.

2) Where did it come from? Reading the comments, I've gathered that the original article contained something about it being constructed by the SCP Foundation on a site that never existed when the Foundation had never created any such thing…The way it is now, however, it's just kind of out-of-nowhere, and no attempts are made to trace its origins or anything. I realize many SCPs' origins are unexplained, but this one kind of cries out for some sort of backstory, or at the very least, a mention of the fact that its origins are unknown.

3) Pretty much what the first ever comment in this discussion page said: If it causes insanity and anxiety within a radius depending on its intensity, how is it that it "terminated" 57 individuals - seemingly by O5 order - without attracting massive amounts of attention and causing extremely high amounts of collateral damage? The first half of the article makes it feel like a super-sniper satellite that actually kills people, and the second half makes it seem like a satellite that shoots lasers to cause spatial abnormalities of varying intensities located where its "target" was that result in insanity and anxiety within a radius based on the intensity, but this is one SCP, and the two halves of the article should add up, not contradict each other.

I'm not downvoting because it's interesting and certainly SCP-worthy; it just needs to be fixed so that it makes some sort of sense (by SCP standards, that is).
